# New accessibility comment documents existing behavior

Reviewed commit: 61e632323dbc6b4a35ed27bf5b9833102ffd5a4e

## TLDR
The terminal text is hidden from assistive technology, but this patch only makes that existing limitation explicit in its comments. It does not introduce the limitation.

## Details
The assigned patch adds the Not built bullet about accessible reading near lines 149-152 and rewrites the comment near lines 347-350. Both sides retain screen.setAttribute("aria-hidden", "true"); there is no changed executable statement. The prior comment already said the rows were decorative and offered no accessible reading. SPEC_impl.md at the reviewed revision, The grid client (1836-1886), describes the existing DOM rendering contract and explicitly leaves composition display unbuilt; it does not establish a newly introduced accessible-reading implementation in this patch. No new functional accessibility regression is supported by this diff.

Suggested bucket: high if reviewing the existing accessibility limitation independently; no new defect in this assigned change. Confidence: confirmed by source; no execution performed. Could-be-highest: false; no security or loss-of-work route established. proposed_drop: outside this change; unchanged aria-hidden implementation and prior explanatory comment in the same hunk. possible_cover: none; coverage sources were not consulted. This disposition does not claim terminal accessibility is adequate.

# New accessibility comment accurately states the existing omission

Reviewed commit: 61e632323dbc6b4a35ed27bf5b9833102ffd5a4e

## TLDR
The new comment accurately warns that terminal text has no accessible reading. That limitation already existed; this change does not conceal it or claim it has been implemented.

## Details
Synthesis revision: checked the changed documentation as an explanatory contract, rather than relying only on the absence of executable changes. The new Not built bullet (149-152) states that terminal text lacks an accessible reading because the rows are aria-hidden. The DOM construction at 343-349 creates the screen and sets aria-hidden=true, and row creation at 617-631 inserts the rendered rows into that screen. The separate textarea at 366-379 is labeled Terminal input and receives browser input; it is not a reading representation of the terminal output. These sources support the new omission statement. Composition is separately and accurately described as committed text only (149-150; input/composition handlers 1527-1544), matching SPEC_impl.md The grid client at 1886. No independent accessibility review was performed.

The original consequence remains: terminal text is hidden from assistive technology, a pre-existing accessibility limitation whose impact may be high. The assigned comment change explicitly documents that limitation and introduces no contradictory accessible-reading promise. Suggested bucket: other for the considered accuracy-of-documentation concern; the original high assessment described the existing accessibility limitation, not a defect in this patch. Confidence: confirmed by source; no execution performed. Could-be-highest: false; no security or loss-of-work route established. proposed_drop: the documentation concern is refuted by the DOM and input responsibilities cited above; this is a proposed disposition only, not a claim that the parent has accepted it. possible_cover: none; coverage sources were not consulted.

event.summary: Removed xterm comparisons retain the operative constraints
event.detail:
# Removed xterm comparisons retain the operative constraints

Reviewed commit: 61e632323dbc6b4a35ed27bf5b9833102ffd5a4e

## TLDR
Removing the repeated xterm comparisons does not remove the rules that preserve terminal behavior. The changed explanation still makes those behaviors Farhelm contracts and preserves the important edge cases beside their implementation.

## Details
Considered whether the rewritten provenance section and deleted comparisons lose constraints needed when changing rendering, selection, history or input. Source checks find the opposite: lines 134-145 explicitly say the behavior is this component’s own contract and changing its details changes what users see. The fixed 80-by-24 fitting reference, padding, scrollbar reserve and authoritative committed drawing size remain explicit at 101-132 and are implemented at 475-499. Selection midpoint tie-breaking remains explicit at 1096-1102; cap trimming preserves column-selection columns at 942-947; per-report selection clearing is explicit at 1632-1643; one wheel message per qualifying event remains explicit at 1816-1826; focus-state reporting on activation remains explicit at 1974-1976. Ports still name their origins locally (positionAt 1081-1083, startSelection 1136-1138, measureChar 419-420), and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md 19-44 maps the retained upstream sources and licenses. No deleted comparison is the sole remaining statement of a concrete behavior in the assigned patch.

Cross-batch interaction checked: the header uses row objects as shorthand for hover evidence (97-99), while the detailed Links section (1243-1257) explicitly distinguishes stable screen-row objects from separate history tokens, and rowIdentityAt (1285-1289) uses model.historyIdentity. grid-model.js 1090-1109 independently decodes history rows and exposes storage-independent tokens. The abbreviated header does not redefine history identity or omit the detailed explanation; it explicitly points to that section. No stale-link/security route is established by this documentation change.

Existing browser test source independently names and checks midpoint selection, cap/anchor preservation, column trimming, input clearing, focus reports, and lazy-history link/reset handling (e2e/grid-client/grid-terminal.spec.ts 827-858, 1186-1252, 1297-1328, 1438-1470, 1541-1610); grid-fit.spec.ts 77-188 retains the history-independent sizing cases. These were source inspections, not executed observations.

Suggested bucket: other for the considered documentation concern. Confidence: confirmed by source. Could-be-highest: false; source checks retain the identity and input constraints and establish no security or loss-of-work route. proposed_drop: refuted by the explicit retained contracts and implementations cited above; no missing operative constraint found. possible_cover: none; excluded coverage sources were not read. This conclusion does not certify historical benchmark numbers or claim every possible behavior has a test.
